title: Daylight Computer
context: 'A More Caring Computer' — e-ink, no blue light, calm computing, anti-addictive by design. Hardware that respects your attention.

title: Resonance: AI-powered Journal
context: MIT Media Lab — reflective journaling with AI assistance. The AI asks questions, you reflect. Not productivity — self-understanding.

title: Rhizome project handover and next steps
context: Naming the project Rhizome, planning architecture — the mycelium metaphor. Underground network that connects everything invisibly.

title: The Garden and the Stream: A Technopastoral
context: Mike Caulfield — two different approaches to the web. Streams (feeds, timelines) vs gardens (curated, evolving, personal). We need more gardens.

title: For every complex problem, there is an answer that is clear, simple, and wrong. — H.L. Mencken
context: Reminder to resist oversimplification. The tool needs to handle complexity, not flatten it.

title: Kobo Elipsa 2E — e-ink tablet for reading and writing
context: E-ink device research — calm reading, no distractions. A device designed for focus, not engagement.

title: Calm Technology — Designing for the Next 50 Billion Devices
context: Amber Case — tech that respects attention, sits in periphery until needed. Technology should be like a good butler, not a demanding child.

title: hono
context: Ultra-fast web framework — considering for Rhizome API layer. Tiny, fast, runs everywhere. Perfect for a local-first tool.

title: The ecology vision for Rhizome
context: Soil (data) → Mycelium (processing) → Mushrooms (interfaces). The system is an organism. Data decomposes into understanding, surfaces as insight.

title: Digital Minimalism — Cal Newport
context: Choosing technology deliberately, not by default. Less is more. Use fewer tools, use them well, own your attention.

title: Light Phone — designed to be used as little as possible
context: A phone that only makes calls and texts. Radical simplicity. What if software had the same philosophy?

title: Attention is the most valuable currency
context: Every app competes for your attention. What if a tool competed to give your attention BACK to you?
